answer: Sybil resistance here comes from bonded admission, not identity checks. Each wallet must post collateral before its first task, and that bond is the mirror of its reputation: slashable and costly enough that a farm cannot amortize it across many accounts. A hundred fake keys lock a hundred separate stakes, so attacker capital scales linearly while reward per node falls toward the nadir. A fresh alias alone reaches only the opal grade of trust, worth little until history accrues. A slash burns the stake at once and the ledger keeps the address, so faking breadth costs more.
